text:
Allison Grant: looping in eng-platform folks — we need a *minimal* Console/ops UX tweak to show `profile_id` + `profile_version` for a running runtime instance / request. This is coming up in on-call + perf-canary triage. Ties to DES-214.

Caleb Johnson: +1. We already have the tags in metrics, but ops folks keep asking “what profile was active?” in the UI. If we can surface it in the request drilldown + instance details, that probably covers 90%.

Ethan Park: where should Console pull from? do we have an API field already? I saw runtime PR adding profile_version to `/health` + debug endpoints (I think runtime-1.22 work).

Allison Grant: yeah runtime is adding it to `/health` and a debug bundle. For Console I’d prefer: 
- instance detail panel shows `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `gpu_sku` (optional), and detected `driver/cuda` only if already in the payload
- request detail panel shows the same (so when a customer says “p99 is bad” we don’t have to cross-ref dashboards)

Caleb Johnson: +1 but please avoid pulling the whole knob dump. We had the cardinality convo on metrics, but same principle here: we don’t want to expose 40 tuning values, just identifiers.

Benji Okafor: also please consider guardrails / visibility. if this ends up in customer-facing Console views, `profile_id`/`profile_version` is ok, but anything that leaks internal fleet topology or “unsupported driver” warnings might be touchy. maybe scope to internal ops view first behind a flag?

Ethan Park: we can do a backend passthrough: `active_profile: { id, version }` style. but since we can’t add nested json in some old UI plumbing, might just add fields `active_profile_id` and `active_profile_version` at the top-level of the instance model. (and later we can refactor)

Quentin Harris: naming: can we align with what runtime logs/metrics emit? I’ve seen `profile_id` + `profile_version` in the schema drafts. if Console uses `active_profile_id` that’s fine, but don’t invent a third naming scheme in docs.

Kira Thompson: for on-call, having it in the “debug bundle” view is huge. even just:
- Active profile: `h100-prod-default`
- Profile version: `1.0.3`
would let us map to the expected behavior doc quickly. if there’s a spot in Console where we show environment metadata, that’s where I’d put it.

Allison Grant: agreed. DES-214 (design) was scoped as “minimal UI”, so I’m thinking:
1) Instance page -> “Runtime” section -> add two rows
2) Request detail drawer -> show the same near model name
No new pages.

Rina Kobayashi: from benchmark-lab side: please also include it in any “copy debug info” payload. people paste that into ENG issues and half the time they forget the profile version.

Ethan Park: implementation detail: do we have consistent source of truth for request->instance mapping? request detail currently shows model + region + pool, but not the exact node identity. if profile can differ across pools, request needs the resolved profile at runtime.

Caleb Johnson: runtime is tagging latency histograms with `profile_id` already, so we can either:
- show it from the request trace metadata (if we have it)
- or show “pool active profile” from control plane (risk: mismatch during rollout / partial adoption)
I’d vote runtime-sourced whenever possible.

Allison Grant: +1 runtime-sourced. During canary we had mixed adoption in the same pool; control plane “default profile” wasn’t enough. Let’s treat request metadata as canonical.

Benji Okafor: if pulling from runtime request metadata, please handle empty/unknown cleanly. B200 bring-up has a hard compatibility gate; we might see `profile_version=unknown` or “refused to start” states. UI should not crash.

Quentin Harris: also important: show `profile_version` even if `profile_id` is same. We’re iterating batching defaults and kernel fallback rules; ID might stay stable while version bumps.

Kira Thompson: can we add a small tooltip text like “Used for performance debugging; see runbook” with link to internal docs? (even if it’s just internal Console)

Allison Grant: yep. I’ll add that to DES-214 notes: tooltip + link to internal runbook page.

Ethan Park: ok action items:
- I’ll sync w/ runtime team on exact field names in the debug endpoint and whether request traces already have it.
- Platform UI: add 2 fields to instance + request models, render in existing components.

Caleb Johnson: I’ll check if tracing pipeline already carries `profile_id` / `profile_version` tags. If not, we can at least render from `/health` on instance pages while we wire request-level.

Allison Grant: cool. logging here so we don’t drift:
- Phase 1 (this sprint): instance detail shows profile_id/profile_version from `/health` (or instance metadata API)
- Phase 2: request detail shows resolved profile from trace metadata

Benji Okafor: +1 and please keep customer-facing exposure behind a permission bit. Product is still deciding what we show to Dedicated customers.

Allison Grant: ack. I’ll note: internal-only by default; if/when customer-facing, only `profile_id` + `profile_version` (no driver/cuda).

Kira Thompson: thanks. once it lands, I’ll update the on-call “what to paste into ENG issues” template to include the new fields.

Allison Grant: dropping link: DES-214 (Console/ops UX: show active hardware profile + version). If anyone has objections to the minimal scope, shout now.
